rubotty admin API (0.8.0)

Download OpenAPI specification:

License: PolyForm Strict License 1.0.0

The REST admin API for rubotty, a multi-tenant chat-bridge and community-moderation platform.

Every response is application/yaml. A request body is either standard form-encoding or application/yaml. Two exceptions: the liveness probe answers plain text, and the room stream answers text/event-stream whose frames each carry a YAML document.

Non-multipart request bodies have a 4 MiB (4,194,304 byte) limit. Both declared Content-Length and bytes read from the request stream are checked; missing or understated length does not allow a larger parsed body. An oversized request returns 413 with the usual YAML error mapping. Multipart file uploads use a policy-derived limit instead, as described on that route.

A bearer API key authenticates every route but the liveness probe. A developer key is confined to a single community. An administrator key is global. Every route a developer key can never reach, whichever community it names, lives under /admin/.

A developer key calling an /admin/ route gets 403, which confirms nothing about whether any particular resource exists. A developer key naming another community's resource gets 404, never 403, so it cannot learn that the resource is real.

The version is the service release this contract was written against.

Health

Unauthenticated liveness.

Liveness probe

Unauthenticated, and the only route that answers anything other than YAML. Returns the plain text ok.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/healthz

Build and runtime facts for either process

Administrator only. source selects which process answers: web (the default, the process serving this request), bot, or all for both. The bot reports its own version and commit rather than this process assuming both containers run the same build. A bot that cannot be reached says so under reachable and error instead of being omitted.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
query Parameters
source
string
Default: "web"
Enum: "web" "bot" "all"

Which process to ask. Anything else is a 400, never a silent fallback.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/debug/info

Recent log lines from either process

Administrator only. Each process keeps its recent lines in a bounded in-memory ring buffer, so this is a live tail and a restart clears it. With source=all both processes' entries merge into one timestamp-sorted list, each tagged with where it came from. A source that cannot be read is reported under errors, so a partial answer is never mistaken for a complete one.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
query Parameters
source
string
Default: "web"
Enum: "web" "bot" "all"

Which process to ask. Anything else is a 400, never a silent fallback.

level
string
Enum: "debug" "info" "warn" "error" "fatal"

This level and anything more severe, rather than an exact match.

limit
integer

How many entries to return, newest first.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/debug/logs

A read-only sweep for a gap the paced backfill's own resume point cannot reach

Administrator only. Runs on the bot process, the only one holding a live platform connection, and is relayed here over the same internal hop debug/logs and debug/info already use. Every backfill-capable channel is swept over its full lookback window with no resume point, and each candidate message is classified as already claimed by the relay ledger, one of this bridge's own relayed copies, older than the safe horizon, or a genuine gap. Nothing here relays, posts or claims anything; it only reports what a real backfill would find. A finding names only the source endpoint, the platform's own message id and its timestamp, never the message itself. An unreachable bot is reported plainly under errors, rather than an empty channel list that would read as "nothing to recover".

Authorizations:
bearerAuth

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/debug/backfill-gaps

Messaging

Posting into a room and watching one live.

Post a message into a room

Enqueues a message for delivery to every platform bridged into the room. Answers 201 with the status queued. A queued message has not yet been delivered. It is screened by the community's moderation settings first, and one they reject is dropped with no further notice here. Reachable with a developer key for its own community. Another community's room answers the same 404 as a room that does not exist.

Another community's room, and a message_id the message map holds nothing for (made up, belonging to a different room, or aged out of the map's TTL), both answer the same 404.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/communities/{slug}/rooms/{room_key}/messages/{message_id}/reactions

Watch a room live, as server-sent events

Server-sent events over the seconds-long buffer the bridge writes at fan-out. Every frame carries a YAML document. SSE joins consecutive data: lines with a newline before the client sees them, so a multi-line YAML document rides one line per frame line and reassembles exactly. Each frame carries an id:, which a browser echoes back as Last-Event-ID on a reconnect. Comment frames beginning : are heartbeats and carry nothing. The first frame arrives immediately with an empty messages list, so a client confirms the stream is live and pins its cursor even on a silent room. There is no backlog to ask for. A subscriber with no cursor starts at the current head, and the buffer prunes within seconds either way. New messages only. An edit, a delete or a reaction takes its own path through the bridge and never reaches this buffer.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

room_key
required
string
Example: general

Which room to act on. Unique within the community, never globally.

query Parameters
since
integer

Resume after this cursor. Omitted, the stream starts at the room's current head. A Last-Event-ID request header does the same thing, which is what makes a browser's automatic reconnect resume cleanly.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/communities/{slug}/rooms/{room_key}/stream

Bridge

A remote system bridged in as a first party platform: posting a message, editing or deleting one, and adding or removing a reaction, each carrying its own real author. Reachable only with an API key scoped to one platform integration.

Post a message from a bridged remote system

Enqueues a message for delivery to every OTHER platform bridged into the same room. Answers 201 with the new message's id, which a later edit, delete or reaction on this same message addresses. Reachable only with an API key scoped to one platform_account (see the API key resource). An ordinary developer or administrator key, a channel_id this account has no mapping for, and another community's slug all answer the same 404.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

channel_id
required
string
Example: support-channel-42

The remote system's OWN identifier for the conversation, exactly as it was given when this channel was mapped into a room. Never a rubotty room_key or endpoint_key.

Request Body schema: application/yaml
required
body
string <= 4000 characters

The message text. May be empty only when at least one attachment is given.

object (BridgeAuthor)

The real person on the remote system who took the action, so a room sees who actually said or did something rather than the integration's own name every time.

reply_to
string

The message_id of an earlier post in this same channel that this one replies to. Omitted for an ordinary message.

Array of objects (BridgeAttachment)

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

There is no create verb anywhere for this resource. A person appears by being observed talking, and is never authored from nothing. Each one carries the names they are bridged as, keyed by the platform each is shown on, which is the same answer the operator dashboard's people page renders.

Set the name this person is bridged as on one platform

The platform in the path is where the name is SHOWN, never where the person was observed, matching the argument the chat command takes. The whole person comes back, so what actually saved can be read rather than assumed. First come wins within a community and platform: a name somebody else already answers to there is refused with 422, as is a name a community that hands out none at all would never have accepted.

Operators

Who may moderate a community, and pending requests to become one.

List the community's operators

Everyone who may moderate here, from both sources, in one list. An entry is either a granted record, which the revoke route can remove, or one of the handles the deployment ships with, which is owner-level in every community and can be removed nowhere. baked_in and removable say which is which on every entry, and the shipped handles come first. Reading only the granted records would report that nobody moderates a community several people do.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/communities/{slug}/operators

Make somebody an operator of this community

Administrator-only, which is the whole reason this write sits under /admin/ while the list above stays on the ordinary community path: reading who runs a community a key already reaches tells that key nothing new, and deciding who runs it is a different thing entirely. Named by platform account rather than by person, since the person may have no record yet; one is created for them, the same way approving their request would. Idempotent: somebody already an operator keeps the record and the scope they have.

Authorizations:

The platform's own id for the account. The reliable half of the name.

username
string

Their handle on that platform, recorded alongside the id when it is known.

display
string

Their display name, used to name a freshly created person record.

Stop somebody operating this community

Refused with 422 for somebody the deployment also ships with as an owner: the record would go while the shipped floor kept handing them the same access here and everywhere else, so the call would read as a revocation and would not be one. Those entries carry removable: false on the list above.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/communities/{slug}/discovered-channels

Propose a room for each discovered, unmapped channel

Works out, by comparing names, which discovered channels match an existing room and which want a new one. Writes nothing, so a client can show the proposals to a human before anything happens. An ambiguous channel, meaning two channels claiming one room or one channel matching two rooms, comes back with the action skip and a reason rather than being left out of the list.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/communities/{slug}/discovered-channels/mapping-proposals

Map the named channels into the named rooms

Applies only the entries in the body, so a caller filters out the proposals it disagrees with. An entry naming a channel that is no longer discovered-and-unmapped is skipped, since a proposal can go stale between reading and applying. Compare applied with requested to see whether that happened. Form encoding carries the list using the usual bracket notation, mappings[][endpoint_key].

https://rubotty.example.org/api/communities/{slug}/discovered-channels/mapping-proposals/apply

Map one discovered channel into a room

The single-channel form of applying a mapping. The bulk apply takes a whole list and skips whatever went stale between reading and submitting; this takes one channel and says plainly when it cannot be mapped.

Name the destination one of three ways: room_key for a room that already exists, or a fresh room under that key; partner for another discovered, unmapped channel to seed a new room alongside; or solo for a room holding this channel alone. Naming none of them is refused.

Mapping enables no feature. The channel is linked into the room's topology and stays as dormant as it was.

A channel that is no longer discovered-and-unmapped answers 404, exactly as one that never existed does.

Spaces the bot was added to that no community owns yet, and the decisions taken on them. Administrator only.

Spaces the bot was added to that no community owns yet

The review queue. A space the bot is added to posts a one-time notice, waits here for a decision, and leaves on its own if none arrives.

Administrator only, and named by no slug, because a pending space belongs to no community: there is nothing for a developer key to be scoped to, and a space awaiting a decision may turn out to be somebody else's.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/pending-spaces/{id}

Drop a refused space, so it may be reviewed again

A refused row stays as a standing refusal: the same space rejoining is turned away without a second review. Clearing it means a later join starts a fresh review.

Only a refused row can be cleared. A row still awaiting a decision is settled through approve or reject instead, and asking to clear one is a 422.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/pending-spaces/{id}

Accept a space onto an existing community, or as a new one

Name an existing community's slug in community, or a name for a brand new community in new_community_name. Naming neither is a 422.

Approving writes the platform connection and nothing else: no room, no channel mapping, no feature. The community stays dormant until somebody maps a channel into a room, so accepting a space never turns anything on by itself.

A space that has already been decided answers 422, and no second decision is recorded.

Refuse a space and leave it

The decision is recorded at once. This process holds no platform connections of its own, so the departure itself is scheduled for whichever bot process is running and lands shortly afterwards.

The row stays as a standing refusal, so the same space rejoining is turned away without a second review, until it is cleared.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/pending-spaces/{id}/reject

Which pending spaces look like they belong to this community

Guesses, by comparing the space's name against the community's name and slug. Nothing here writes and nothing here decides: a suggestion is accepted by approving that pending space.

The matching is deliberately mean, since attaching a stranger's group to somebody's community is far worse than showing no suggestion at all. A space that matches two communities is suggested to neither, and a space that matches none is still in the review queue.

Administrator only, because a pending space belongs to no community and a guess about one is still a look at somebody else's space.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/communities/{slug}/features/{feature}

Set the community-wide default's enabled state and config

A body may set enabled alone, config alone, or both in one request. Each config key runs through the same coercion a command-line or dashboard edit takes: booleans, numbers, comma lists, explicit JSON, or a plain string. The response is the resulting row.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

feature
required
string
Example: word_filter

Which feature to act on. An unknown name is refused.

Request Body schema:
optional
enabled
boolean

Turn the feature on or off for this scope.

object

A feature's settings for one scope, as a mapping from a config key to its value. A value is an ordinary scalar, list or mapping, matching the type the key declares: a duration is either a plain number of seconds or a string such as "24 hours", and a key declared as a choice carries one of its permitted strings.

Which keys a given feature takes, their types, their defaults and the values they are restricted to are deliberately NOT enumerated here. They belong to the release a deployment is actually running, while this document is read beside deployments on other releases, so a copy here would describe some other deployment's features as though they were yours. GET /features/schema answers for the deployment being talked to, from the same declarations the operator dashboard builds its per-feature config form from; look up the entry whose name matches this row's feature.

The mapping is open for a second reason as well: a scope can still hold a key from a release where the feature declared it and this one does not, and that key is reported here rather than hidden.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/communities/{slug}/features/{feature}

Only what has been set for this room, rather than the value it would resolve to at runtime by inheriting the community default. A room with no override for a feature is absent from this list.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/communities/{slug}/rooms/{room_key}/features

Read what a feature resolves to for one room

What is actually in force for this room: its own override when it has one, otherwise the community-wide default it falls back to. inherited says which of the two answered, and room_key names the room asked about either way.

The list beside this one answers a different question, namely what has been set on the room explicitly, so a room with no override of its own is simply absent from it.

404 only when neither the room nor the community has ever configured the feature.

Every feature's declared config shape

What config accepts for each feature: the same schema the dashboard reads to build its per-feature config form, restated as data. Deployment-wide rather than community-scoped, since the shape is identical for every community: no slug is named, and a developer key reads it the same way an administrator key does.

This is the authority on config keys, and the only one. The static document deliberately describes config as an open mapping rather than copying these shapes into itself, because the shapes belong to the release a deployment is running and this answer comes from the deployment being talked to.

Content policy

What the model-backed content policy check did, and the matches an operator reversed and kept as samples for improving a policy's wording.

Read the content policy actions an operator reversed

One row per mistake an operator named, newest first: an action undone with /vindicate, or a message /condemn said the policies should have caught. Each carries the text, the model's own reasoning and confidence, and the operator's stated reason, which together are what a policy description gets rewritten against. Read kind to tell the two apart. No author is recorded: the corpus is about the text and the judgement.

Every file this community is holding

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/files

Store a file and receive the UUID that names it

The one route in this API that takes multipart/form-data. The file is streamed into storage, compressed and encrypted, and is never held whole. The community's own settings apply rather than any deployment default: whether it accepts files at all, how long it keeps them, and how large one may be. An administrator key is not a way around a setting an operator made. This multipart route is exempt from the 4 MiB text-body limit. Before parsing, the complete request is bounded by the largest configured file cap for the community, including room overrides, plus 64 KiB (65,536 bytes) of multipart overhead. The selected room or community file policy is then enforced on the file itself. uuid comes back here and from a rotation. It is not stored and cannot be asked for again. A caller that does not keep it can still see the file in a listing and expire it by id.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

Request Body schema: multipart/form-data
required

The one multipart body in this API, exempt from the 4 MiB text-body limit. The complete request is bounded by the largest configured file cap for the community, including room overrides, plus 64 KiB (65,536 bytes) of multipart overhead. Storage also enforces the file cap selected by room_key, or the community default when it is absent.

file
required
string <binary>

The file itself. Streamed, so its size is bounded only by the community's cap.

room_key
string

Which room the file belongs to. Optional, and used to resolve the room's own settings where they differ from the community's.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/files

Replace a file's link, retiring the old one

Give it the UUID you hold and it answers with a new one. The old link stops working the moment this returns, which is what a leaked link needs. The UUID has to be supplied because only its digest is stored. This is a real re-encryption: the file is unsealed with the old secret and written out again under a new one, so the time it takes grows with the file. It is streamed, so it is not also expensive in memory. The expiry is left where it was, so rotating changes who can reach a file and leaves its retention alone. A UUID that names nothing live and a UUID naming another community's file both answer 404.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

Request Body schema:
required

The UUID naming the file to act on.

uuid
required
string <uuid>

The UUID naming the file. An absent one is refused rather than read as "no such file".

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/files/rotate

Mark a file for deletion on the next reclaim pass

Give it the UUID you hold and the file's expiry moves to now. The link stops working straight away, since a download only resolves a file whose expiry is still ahead of it, and the bytes go when the deployment next reclaims storage. Unlike a rotation this needs no key material, so the digest of the UUID is enough to find the file. The same 404 covers a UUID that names nothing live and one naming another community's file.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

Request Body schema:
required

The UUID naming the file to act on.

uuid
required
string <uuid>

The UUID naming the file. An absent one is refused rather than read as "no such file".

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/files/expire

Read one file's record

Addressed by the id a listing gives, since the UUID is not stored and cannot be used to look anything up. Carries no link, like the listing.

bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

id
required
integer

Which record to act on, as the id the matching list route reports.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/files/{id}

Mark a file for deletion without holding its UUID

The same effect as the expire call, addressed by the id a listing gives instead of by the UUID, which makes it the only way to act on a file whose UUID nobody kept. Expiring touches no key material: the expiry is a stored field, and the bytes go when the deployment next reclaims storage. Rotation has no equivalent, since rotating has to unseal the file and so needs the secret. Calling it twice is harmless. A file already past its expiry is left where it is rather than having its deletion pushed further out.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

id
required
integer

Which record to act on, as the id the matching list route reports.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/files/{id}

Grant viewer status to a handle

Binds the grant to the platform's stable native user identifier. Supply native_id, or name a handle with exactly one identity already observed by this deployment. A full Matrix ID or scoped IRC account may identify itself; unknown or ambiguous handles are refused with 422. Repeating a grant for the same platform and native identity answers the existing entry. Tokens

Credentials somebody is handed so that sending one to the bot grants them a role. Shown once when minted, spent on first use, revocable until then.

List every token that hands somebody a role

Every token this deployment has, community scoped ones included, since an administrator is who has to be able to account for all of them. The token strings themselves are not here and cannot be: only their digests are kept.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/auth-tokens

Mint a token that hands over reading every community

Administrator only, because the token IS the grant: it is taken in advance, so anything a developer key could mint here would go around the check on handing that role over directly. A token minted for one community belongs on that community's own path instead.

The answer carries the token string, and it is the only time it is ever readable. Whoever holds it is granted the role by sending the bot /auth and the string, once, before it expires.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
Request Body schema:
optional
ttl_seconds
integer

How long it stays redeemable. Defaults to a day, and a fortnight is the most it may be.

label
string

A note about who it is for, so a list of them is readable later.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/auth-tokens

Take a token back before it is used

Refused with 422 once the token has been redeemed. The role it carried is already granted by then, so revoking it would say something untrue; take the role itself back instead.

bearerAuth

required
string

The token's public identifier. Never the token string itself, which is not stored.

Mint a token that hands over a role in this community

Operator here, viewer here, or both, and at least one of the two. The scope is the path's: nothing in the body can widen a token past this community, which is why an operator of it may mint one.

A developer key may hand over the viewer, which changes nothing here. Handing over operator is refused with 422 for a developer key and needs an administrator key, because a developer key is read-write inside one community without being an operator of it, and a token making a human operator would reach past what the key holds.

The answer carries the token string, and it is the only time it is ever readable. Whoever holds it is granted the role by sending the bot /auth and the string, once, before it expires.

Backfill

What a gap sweep held back instead of sending, per channel, and the decision it is waiting on. Administrator only.

What a sweep held back, waiting on a decision

A gap larger than the channel's own auto-relay limit is written down rather than sent, per channel, and goes out only when somebody accepts it. This is that list.

Every row carries the counts the sweep recorded. ours is the one to read first: it is how many of the fetched messages the sweep recognised as this bridge's own relayed copies and skipped. A zero there on a channel that has bridged for months means the ownership check is not working, and accepting anything would push those copies back into a live room.

Administrator only, and named by no slug: one sweep writes proposals across a community's channels, and accepting one posts into live rooms.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
query Parameters
state
string
Default: "pending"
Enum: "pending" "approved" "rejected" "expired" "relayed" "all"

Which proposals to list. pending is waiting on a decision, approved is accepted and waiting for the bot to finish sending it, relayed has gone out, rejected was refused, and expired ran out of time undecided. all merges every state into one ordering. Anything else is a 400, never a silent fallback.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/backfill-proposals

Read one proposal and the messages it would send

The stored list, exactly as an accept would relay it: nothing is recomputed here or at accept time, so what is read is what goes.

A preview is kept only while the proposal still needs one. Once the proposal is rejected, expires, or has had its accepted list relayed, the previews are deleted and the row keeps the counts alone. That case answers items_pruned: true with a note saying so, rather than an empty list that would read as "the sweep was going to send nothing".

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
id
required
integer

Which record to act on, as the id the matching list route reports.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/backfill-proposals/{id}

Accept one channel's list, and send it

Accepting stamps the proposal and hands the stored list to the bot process, which is the only one holding the platform connections that can send. The send itself is paced and runs there, so this answers as soon as the bot has taken the list rather than when the last message has landed.

relaying is whether the bot took it. False means the proposal is accepted but nothing is going out, with the reason under errors.

Only a proposal still waiting on a decision can be accepted. One already decided, or one that has run out of time, answers 422 and no second decision is recorded.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
id
required
integer

Which record to act on, as the id the matching list route reports.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/backfill-proposals/{id}/approve

Refuse one channel's list

Nothing from that channel is sent, and the previews go with the decision. The row stays, with its counts, so the history still says what was proposed and what happened to it.

Only a proposal still waiting on a decision can be refused; one already decided answers 422.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
id
required
integer

Which record to act on, as the id the matching list route reports.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/backfill-proposals/{id}/reject

List the deployment-wide ceiling on what an operator may change

Administrator only. One row per action in the catalog: a toggle and a configure grant per feature, plus a handful of whole-section grants (moderate_user, manage_rooms, manage_discovered, manage_operator_requests, manage_redirection, manage_alerts, manage_webhooks, manage_participation). Governs every community identically, it is not a per-community setting. An individual operator's own grant (see /communities/{slug}/operators) narrows within whatever this allows; it can never widen past it. The same table the dashboard's Operators page checkbox grid reads and writes.

Administrator only. A full replace, not a merge: every action in the catalog is set from this one body. Sending only the actions meant to end up writable is the normal shape of a call here.

Every token this deployment has, community scoped ones included, since an administrator is who has to be able to account for all of them. The token strings themselves are not here and cannot be: only their digests are kept.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/auth-tokens

Mint a token that hands over reading every community

Administrator only, because the token IS the grant: it is taken in advance, so anything a developer key could mint here would go around the check on handing that role over directly. A token minted for one community belongs on that community's own path instead.

The answer carries the token string, and it is the only time it is ever readable. Whoever holds it is granted the role by sending the bot /auth and the string, once, before it expires.

bearerAuth

optional

integer

How long it stays redeemable. Defaults to a day, and a fortnight is the most it may be.

label
string

A note about who it is for, so a list of them is readable later.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

Spaces the bot was added to that no community owns yet

The review queue. A space the bot is added to posts a one-time notice, waits here for a decision, and leaves on its own if none arrives.

Administrator only, and named by no slug, because a pending space belongs to no community: there is nothing for a developer key to be scoped to, and a space awaiting a decision may turn out to be somebody else's.

Drop a refused space, so it may be reviewed again

A refused row stays as a standing refusal: the same space rejoining is turned away without a second review. Clearing it means a later join starts a fresh review.

Only a refused row can be cleared. A row still awaiting a decision is settled through approve or reject instead, and asking to clear one is a 422.

Accept a space onto an existing community, or as a new one

Name an existing community's slug in community, or a name for a brand new community in new_community_name. Naming neither is a 422.

Approving writes the platform connection and nothing else: no room, no channel mapping, no feature. The community stays dormant until somebody maps a channel into a room, so accepting a space never turns anything on by itself.

A space that has already been decided answers 422, and no second decision is recorded.

bearerAuth

new_community_name
string

A name for a brand new community to create for the space. Its slug is derived from the name and made unique.

boolean

Promote whoever added the bot to operator of the community. Does nothing when can_make_operator is false.

Refuse a space and leave it

The decision is recorded at once. This process holds no platform connections of its own, so the departure itself is scheduled for whichever bot process is running and lands shortly afterwards.

The row stays as a standing refusal, so the same space rejoining is turned away without a second review, until it is cleared.

Which pending spaces look like they belong to this community

Guesses, by comparing the space's name against the community's name and slug. Nothing here writes and nothing here decides: a suggestion is accepted by approving that pending space.

The matching is deliberately mean, since attaching a stranger's group to somebody's community is far worse than showing no suggestion at all. A space that matches two communities is suggested to neither, and a space that matches none is still in the review queue.

Administrator only, because a pending space belongs to no community and a guess about one is still a look at somebody else's space.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/webhooks

Subscribe an address to this community's events

The response carries the signing secret. Keep it: every delivery is signed with it, and no other call shows the value again. Rotating replaces it. Deliveries follow the Standard Webhooks conventions. Each request carries webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature, and the signature is computed over id.timestamp.body with HMAC-SHA256, so any off-the-shelf Standard Webhooks library verifies it. The body is YAML. Delivery is at least once, so a subscriber should deduplicate on webhook-id. Events reach one subscription in the order they happened.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

Request Body schema:
required
url
required
string

Where deliveries are sent. Has to be https.

required
string or Array of strings

Which events to send. An unknown one is refused here, which is the only point it is checked.

room_key
string

Narrow to one room. Omitted, every room in the community is sent.

label
string

What this subscription is for. Optional.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

Stop sending to this address

Removes the subscription and its delivery history together. Anything still queued for it is dropped rather than sent.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/webhooks/{public_id}

Replace the signing secret, with an overlap

Mints a new signing secret and returns it. Until the overlap lapses every delivery is signed with both the new secret and the old one, and carries both in the one space-delimited webhook-signature header the Standard Webhooks format defines for this, so the receiving end keeps verifying with the old secret until the new one is deployed. An overlap of 0 retires the old secret immediately, which is what a leaked secret calls for.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

public_id
required
string

The subscription's public identifier. Not the signing secret.

Request Body schema:
optional
overlap
integer

Seconds the outgoing secret keeps working. Defaults to 86400. Zero retires it at once.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/webhooks/{public_id}/rotate

One row per event per subscription, newest first, with the response code or the error behind each one. A queued delivery has attempts left and is waiting out a backoff. A failed one has exhausted them and is not tried again.

Enum: "queued" "delivered" "failed"

Narrow to one subscription, by its public id.

Default: 200

How many attempts to return, newest first.

Responses

Every file this community is holding

Newest first. No entry carries a UUID or a download link, since neither is recoverable from what is stored. A caller that has lost a file's UUID can no longer reach or rotate that file, though it can still be expired by id.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/files

Store a file and receive the UUID that names it

The one route in this API that takes multipart/form-data. The file is streamed into storage, compressed and encrypted, and is never held whole. The community's own settings apply rather than any deployment default: whether it accepts files at all, how long it keeps them, and how large one may be. An administrator key is not a way around a setting an operator made. This multipart route is exempt from the 4 MiB text-body limit. Before parsing, the complete request is bounded by the largest configured file cap for the community, including room overrides, plus 64 KiB (65,536 bytes) of multipart overhead. The selected room or community file policy is then enforced on the file itself. uuid comes back here and from a rotation. It is not stored and cannot be asked for again. A caller that does not keep it can still see the file in a listing and expire it by id.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

Request Body schema: multipart/form-data
required

The one multipart body in this API, exempt from the 4 MiB text-body limit. The complete request is bounded by the largest configured file cap for the community, including room overrides, plus 64 KiB (65,536 bytes) of multipart overhead. Storage also enforces the file cap selected by room_key, or the community default when it is absent.

file
required
string <binary>

The file itself. Streamed, so its size is bounded only by the community's cap.

room_key
string

Which room the file belongs to. Optional, and used to resolve the room's own settings where they differ from the community's.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/files

Replace a file's link, retiring the old one

Give it the UUID you hold and it answers with a new one. The old link stops working the moment this returns, which is what a leaked link needs. The UUID has to be supplied because only its digest is stored. This is a real re-encryption: the file is unsealed with the old secret and written out again under a new one, so the time it takes grows with the file. It is streamed, so it is not also expensive in memory. The expiry is left where it was, so rotating changes who can reach a file and leaves its retention alone. A UUID that names nothing live and a UUID naming another community's file both answer 404.

required

The UUID naming the file to act on.

uuid
required
string <uuid>

The UUID naming the file. An absent one is refused rather than read as "no such file".

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/files/rotate

Mark a file for deletion on the next reclaim pass

Give it the UUID you hold and the file's expiry moves to now. The link stops working straight away, since a download only resolves a file whose expiry is still ahead of it, and the bytes go when the deployment next reclaims storage. Unlike a rotation this needs no key material, so the digest of the UUID is enough to find the file. The same 404 covers a UUID that names nothing live and one naming another community's file.

Mark a file for deletion without holding its UUID

The same effect as the expire call, addressed by the id a listing gives instead of by the UUID, which makes it the only way to act on a file whose UUID nobody kept. Expiring touches no key material: the expiry is a stored field, and the bytes go when the deployment next reclaims storage. Rotation has no equivalent, since rotating has to unseal the file and so needs the secret. Calling it twice is harmless. A file already past its expiry is left where it is rather than having its deletion pushed further out.

Build and runtime facts for either process

Administrator only. source selects which process answers: web (the default, the process serving this request), bot, or all for both. The bot reports its own version and commit rather than this process assuming both containers run the same build. A bot that cannot be reached says so under reachable and error instead of being omitted.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/debug/info

Recent log lines from either process

Administrator only. Each process keeps its recent lines in a bounded in-memory ring buffer, so this is a live tail and a restart clears it. With source=all both processes' entries merge into one timestamp-sorted list, each tagged with where it came from. A source that cannot be read is reported under errors, so a partial answer is never mistaken for a complete one.

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/debug/logs

A read-only sweep for a gap the paced backfill's own resume point cannot reach

Administrator only. Runs on the bot process, the only one holding a live platform connection, and is relayed here over the same internal hop debug/logs and debug/info already use. Every backfill-capable channel is swept over its full lookback window with no resume point, and each candidate message is classified as already claimed by the relay ledger, one of this bridge's own relayed copies, older than the safe horizon, or a genuine gap. Nothing here relays, posts or claims anything; it only reports what a real backfill would find. A finding names only the source endpoint, the platform's own message id and its timestamp, never the message itself. An unreachable bot is reported plainly under errors, rather than an empty channel list that would read as "nothing to recover".

Authorizations:
bearerAuth

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/debug/backfill-gaps

What a sweep held back, waiting on a decision

A gap larger than the channel's own auto-relay limit is written down rather than sent, per channel, and goes out only when somebody accepts it. This is that list.

Every row carries the counts the sweep recorded. ours is the one to read first: it is how many of the fetched messages the sweep recognised as this bridge's own relayed copies and skipped. A zero there on a channel that has bridged for months means the ownership check is not working, and accepting anything would push those copies back into a live room.

Administrator only, and named by no slug: one sweep writes proposals across a community's channels, and accepting one posts into live rooms.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
query Parameters
state
string
Default: "pending"
Enum: "pending" "approved" "rejected" "expired" "relayed" "all"

Which proposals to list. pending is waiting on a decision, approved is accepted and waiting for the bot to finish sending it, relayed has gone out, rejected was refused, and expired ran out of time undecided. all merges every state into one ordering. Anything else is a 400, never a silent fallback.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/backfill-proposals

Read one proposal and the messages it would send

The stored list, exactly as an accept would relay it: nothing is recomputed here or at accept time, so what is read is what goes.

A preview is kept only while the proposal still needs one. Once the proposal is rejected, expires, or has had its accepted list relayed, the previews are deleted and the row keeps the counts alone. That case answers items_pruned: true with a note saying so, rather than an empty list that would read as "the sweep was going to send nothing".

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
id
required
integer

Which record to act on, as the id the matching list route reports.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/backfill-proposals/{id}

Accept one channel's list, and send it

Accepting stamps the proposal and hands the stored list to the bot process, which is the only one holding the platform connections that can send. The send itself is paced and runs there, so this answers as soon as the bot has taken the list rather than when the last message has landed.

relaying is whether the bot took it. False means the proposal is accepted but nothing is going out, with the reason under errors.

Only a proposal still waiting on a decision can be accepted. One already decided, or one that has run out of time, answers 422 and no second decision is recorded.

Nothing from that channel is sent, and the previews go with the decision. The row stays, with its counts, so the history still says what was proposed and what happened to it.

Only a proposal still waiting on a decision can be refused; one already decided answers 422.

Webhooks

List where this community's events are sent

A subscription is a standing instruction to forward what happens in a community's rooms to an address outside this deployment. The signing secret is never in this response: it is returned when the subscription is created and when it is rotated, and at no other time.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/webhooks

Subscribe an address to this community's events

The response carries the signing secret. Keep it: every delivery is signed with it, and no other call shows the value again. Rotating replaces it. Deliveries follow the Standard Webhooks conventions. Each request carries webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature, and the signature is computed over id.timestamp.body with HMAC-SHA256, so any off-the-shelf Standard Webhooks library verifies it. The body is YAML. Delivery is at least once, so a subscriber should deduplicate on webhook-id. Events reach one subscription in the order they happened.

Authorizations:
bearerAuth
path Parameters
slug
required
string
Example: sample

Which community to act on. A developer key may only name its own.

Request Body schema:
required
url
required
string

Where deliveries are sent. Has to be https.

required
string or Array of strings

Which events to send. An unknown one is refused here, which is the only point it is checked.

room_key
string

Narrow to one room. Omitted, every room in the community is sent.

label
string

What this subscription is for. Optional.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

Replace the signing secret, with an overlap

Mints a new signing secret and returns it. Until the overlap lapses every delivery is signed with both the new secret and the old one, and carries both in the one space-delimited webhook-signature header the Standard Webhooks format defines for this, so the receiving end keeps verifying with the old secret until the new one is deployed. An overlap of 0 retires the old secret immediately, which is what a leaked secret calls for.

Request Body schema:
optional
overlap
integer

Seconds the outgoing secret keeps working. Defaults to 86400. Zero retires it at once.

Responses

Production (mounted under the unified web surface)

https://rubotty.example.org/api/admin/communities/{slug}/webhooks/{public_id}/rotate
